LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD builds the `resticprofile` Go application from its official upstream GitHub repository (`git+https://github.com/creativeprojects/resticprofile.git`), pinned to the tag `v$pkgver`. The source is consistent with the package's stated purpose (a configuration profile manager and scheduler for restic backup).

The `prepare()` and `build()` functions perform standard Go module operations: `go mod download` and a `go build` with conventional `-ldflags` to inject version/commit/date metadata into the binary. The `package()` function installs the binary, license, documentation, examples, systemd contrib files, and shell completions into the appropriate system paths — all routine packaging steps.

The base64-encoded string in the maintainer line (`eXUzYWN0eHQydHR0ZmlteEBjaHllbi5jYwo=`) is simply an obfuscation of the maintainer's email address (`yan@...`), a common anti-scraping technique used by AUR maintainers to hide their contact info from automated email harvesters. It is not an obfuscated command or payload — no execution, decoding-for-eval, or exfiltration pattern is present.

The `sha256sums` entry contains a hash rather than `SKIP` for a VCS source, which is unconventional but not malicious. No suspicious downloads, network exfiltration, encoded payloads, or unexpected file operations are present.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
